title: Crash on loading a new scene after playing a long time caused by `Cannot get class ''.`
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.4.1.stable.mono.official.49a5bc7b6
- Not reproducible in: 3.x

### System information

Windows 10, but might also affect other platforms but as most of our players are on Windows it might be the case that not enough players are on Linux to have seen this problem there

### Issue description

I think I have basically the same bug as: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/106934 but as I cannot open a close issue back up I'm making this new one.

So basically ever since we updated our game to Godot 4 over a year ago, we have been having players report very weird scene loading issues that start happening after playing for some time, likely at least a few hours. The first thing we saw was that scenes that loaded perfectly fine thousands of times, for some reason randomly had C# export variables be suddenly null. I opened an issue for that but it has not been solved: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/93083

Next we did the only thing we could: we removed all NodePath usages from our code that we could. Thanks to this it seems like the rare problems related to NodePaths being null is now gone. Sadly however that has been replaced with this new issue. So now instead of players encountering a partly loaded scene where the game is basically softlocked, the game now crashes with a log like:


The game crashes when trying to switch game scenes. The key part seems to be that loading a scene file that usually works totally fine, for some reason starts to fail after playing for some hours. We are getting now about as many of these new full crash reports as we used to get reports about the earlier NodePath issue. We switched a softlock in the game for a hard crash by trying to avoid the NodePath feature. So I kind of suspect there's some common underlying cause that eventually causes Godot to no longer be able to load .tscn files correctly. This might be a Windows specific problem, but that could also be just an effect of that we have way more players on Windows than other platforms so they get the most playtime and thus encounter this random problem the most.

### Steps to reproduce

- Play an exported Godot game for a few hours
- Suddenly when the game is trying to load a new scene to switch to during gameplay see that the game suddenly crashes
- Check the game output and notice that the crash begins with always this message: `Cannot get class ''.`

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I don't think it is possible to make a minimum reproduction project due to the random nature of this bug and how it takes hours to trigger the problem. But I know that this Thrive release (at least the Windows version) can crash due to this problem: https://github.com/Revolutionary-Games/Thrive/releases/tag/v0.8.3
